The drug 2-methoxyestradiol is directly linked to UDP-glucuronosyltransferase 2B10, an enzyme that is targeted by Difengpiol A. This enzyme, in turn, acts as a target for G2/mitotic-specific cyclin B1. The integration of these relationships implies that 2-methoxyestradiol may modulate the activity of UDP-glucuronosyltransferase 2B10, which could then influence the expression or function of G2/mitotic-specific cyclin B1. This mechanism highlights a possible regulatory role of 2-methoxyestradiol in the G2 phase of the cell cycle, potentially through the modulation of cyclin B1 expression. The evidence suggests a complex, multi-step interaction involving enzyme targeting and cyclin regulation, which may be critical for cellular processes related to mitosis.
